newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, swaps up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, swaps up in late trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday as swap rates were seen edging up further, dealers said.
They said overall trading was slow but some dollar selling from Singapore operators seemed have brought the rate closer to the central bank's floor rate.
One U.S. bank dealer said there were some big orders to sell dollars from Singapore in the afternoon but the U.S. currency was well supported at the 2,321.25 level.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,321.0/21.5 at 0845 GMT against an opening of 2,322.5/23.00.
Dealers said trading was in a narrow-range but some profit taking on dollars helped limit any further downside.
The U.S. bank dealer said the selling of dollars might be due to preparations for weekend payments.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,320.30/20.90 and 2,320.25/20.75, respectively.
He said expensive short-dated swaps, possibly on worry over liquidity outlook, had driven longer-term rates up. Overnight swap was at 0.65/0.70 and tom/next at 0.70/0.80 points.
"The swap market seemed to neglect liquidity condition. We have sufficient rupiah but swaps remained high." he said.
One local bank dealer said swaps covering by joint-venture and foreign banks appeared to have driven short-dated swaps up.
Dealers said high swaps had also forced offshore operators to cut long dollars positions.
One-month swap rose to 20.25/20.50 from 19.0/20.0, two to 35.5/37.0 from 34.50/35.25, three to 53.5/55.0 from 52.25/53.50 and six to 103.50/104.75 from 102.0/104.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,318/2,510 and the conversion rate at 2,318/2,366 on Tuesday.
